title: Distributive Property: From a(b+c) to Combining Terms
preview: Walk from 3(x + 2) through negative coefficients and fractional coefficients, then combine like terms after distributing. Enrichment goes the other direction — factoring.

body.goal: Students see the distributive property as 'multiply each term inside by the outside number,' robust across negatives, fractional coefficients, and follow-up combining of like terms — and recognize the inverse move (factoring).
body.launch: Run the warm-up so the basic multiplication facts are hot. Then start the slice. Don't pre-teach 'distribute to both terms' — let the early steps make it obvious.
body.prerequisiteLabel: Warm up with quick multiplication so the distributive step itself is the only new move.

steps.teacherNote: Anchor — distribute the 3 to each term inside.
Negative inside the parens — does the structure change?
Negative coefficient outside. Watch for sign mistakes.
Two negatives. Pause: 'why does the +10 come out positive?' Sign management is the move.
Variable term has its own coefficient — multiply 4 × 2.
Fractional coefficient. Make sure they multiply the fraction by *each* term.
Distribute, then combine the like x-terms.
Two distributions, then combine. The big one.

enrichmentSteps.teacherNote: Inverse move. Find the GCF (3) and pull it out front.

body.consolidation: Pull it together: 'When we distribute, what are we doing? When we factor, what are we doing?' Get a class statement that names them as opposite moves. Then ask: 'On step 5, why did we get +10 not -10? On step 7, what would have happened if we forgot to multiply the fraction by both terms?'
